# paper-finder-student-mcp

> Academic paper search MCP server through OpenAlex. No key needed. Free and open source MCP server for AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and others).

## Setup
- Run with npx -y paper-finder-student-mcp
- No key or account. Optional OPENALEX_EMAIL for OpenAlex's polite pool.
- Papers are identified by DOI (10.xxxx/yyy) or OpenAlex id (W followed by digits).

## Data
- All results come from OpenAlex (https://openalex.org), a free open catalog of more than 250 million works, so the papers are real, not invented.
- Every tool reads OpenAlex directly, so there is no key needed and no account.

## Tools
- search_papers: Search scholarly papers by keywords. Returns title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI and a free to read link when one exists. Inputs: query (required keywords), from_year (optional earliest publication year), open_access_only (optional, false by default), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'find open access papers on spaced repetition since 2020.'
- get_paper: Details for one paper, including the abstract and a free to read link when one exists. A wrong or unknown reference returns a not found error that suggests searching by title or checking the DOI format. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807). Example prompt: 'show me the abstract of DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'
- get_paper_by_doi: Details for one paper looked up by DOI only, including the abstract and a free to read link when one exists. An OpenAlex id or a malformed DOI returns an invalid ref error that points at get_paper. Inputs: doi (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link). Example prompt: 'get the paper with DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'
- find_open_access_pdf: Finds a free to read copy of one paper and returns the link, preferring a PDF over a landing page. When OpenAlex has no free copy it says so in plain words instead of failing. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807). Example prompt: 'find a free PDF of this paper, DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'
- related_papers: Papers that OpenAlex lists as related to a given paper. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers are related to DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'
- get_related_work: Other papers on the same topic as one paper. Returns the same list as related_papers, kept as a verb-first name for clients that prefer it. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what related work should I read for DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'
- cited_by: Newer papers that cite a given paper, most recent first. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'who cited DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'
- list_author_papers: Papers by one author, most cited first. Matches the author name as it is written on the papers, so exact spelling matters. Inputs: author (required, the name as it appears on the paper, for example Jane Doe), from_year (optional earliest publication year), open_access_only (optional, false by default), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'list papers by John Dewey on education since 1950.'

Each tool description states its inputs and one example prompt.
